visual_action: The video opens with a shot of the Statue of Liberty against a clear blue sky, followed by shots of American flags waving in the wind. It then transitions into a montage of various scenes: a female figure skater performing on an ice rink with the Olympic rings visible, a rocket launching into the sky, an aerial shot of a large canyon with a river (Horseshoe Bend), a large crowd of people marching in a city street protest, a jumbotron at a crowded stadium displaying a message, a musical group with Puerto Rican and American flags performing, and a final shot of an American flag.

cast.name: Democratic Party
cast.evidence: The video was posted by the @democrats account.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: The video directly references and refutes his signature slogan, "make America great again".

cast.name: Make America Great Again (MAGA) movement
cast.evidence: The speaker and on-screen text quote the slogan "make America great again".

spoken_summary: A male narrator contrasts two viewpoints. He states, "Some people say, 'make America great again.'" He then offers a rebuttal: "I say America was great all along. Some of us just forgot why."
audio_music: The video begins with male narration. After the narration concludes around the 9-second mark, an uplifting and inspiring instrumental track featuring acoustic guitar begins and plays through the rest of the montage, creating a patriotic and hopeful mood.
editing_pacing: The video is a montage with a series of relatively quick cuts between different B-roll clips, paced to the music.
cultural_references: Prince (implied by a 'LETS GO CRAZY' billboard near the 'FIRST AVENUE' music venue in Minneapolis)
central_claim: America has always been great, and the idea that it needs to be made 'great again' is a false premise.
intended_effect: To instill a sense of patriotism and pride in America's existing strengths and diversity, and to counter the narrative of national decline.
